Information since the August meeting points to a strong labor market and solid real activity with inflation near 2 percent and expectations little changed. The decision to raise the target range to 2–2.25 percent and set IOER at 2.20 percent is consistent with rule-based and forward-looking frameworks from the monetary policy literature: a Taylor-rule-style response to positive output and labor market gaps with inflation near target, and the Clarida–Galí–Gertler view of gradual, forward-looking stabilization. The emphasis on “further gradual increases” reflects documented interest-rate smoothing behavior. Operationally, relying on IOER and ON RRP to control the funds rate accords with the implementation approach discussed by Goodfriend (2002). With inflation expectations anchored and risks “roughly balanced,” the statement supports credibility in line with Romer and Romer’s evidence on anti-inflation commitments, while balance sheet runoff and guidance shape longer-term yields consistent with Cochrane–Piazzesi term structure insights. Net assessment: confident about growth and employment, mildly hawkish on policy.
